outcome: No case, bound, or resolution of Hartshorne's conjecture(s) as stated in this bullet has changed since 26 January 2024; the two nearby 2024-2026 papers found are either an adjacent classification problem (not a case of the conjecture) or a conditional implication involving a separate conjecture, and neither settles any part of Hartshorne's own conjectures.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet 'Hartshorne's conjectures' (plural, unlinked, citing a single footnote to Hartshorne's own 1974 paper) refers to the family of conjectures Robin Hartshorne proposed, of which the best-known and most actively worked on is the complete-intersection conjecture: a smooth, nondegenerate, codimension-c subvariety X of P^n with n >= 2c+1 (equivalently c < n/3) is a complete intersection. (Hartshorne also stated a conjecture on ample subvarieties/submanifolds intersecting, related to work on the Frankel conjecture; no activity was found on that variant either in the window.) Multiple 2024-2026 surveys and papers (ProofAtlas's dedicated tracking page, the arXiv listing, Arrondo's survey) confirm the main conjecture remains fully open, including in the much-studied codimension-2 / Fano case. Two items surfaced during triage and further search are close to the topic but do not change the bullet: (1) Watanabe's 'Quadratic Varieties of Small Codimension' (arXiv:2405.04002, received 28 Jan 2025, published SIGMA 15 Jun 2025) proves the conjecture for quadratic varieties (a case already settled pre-2024 by Ionescu-Russo) and then classifies the *boundary-adjacent* case n=2c-1, which sits just outside the conjectured range n>=2c+1 -- this is a related classification exercise near the conjecture's edge, not a restriction of the conjecture's own statement, so under the scope rule (§3.1) it is a related problem rather than a case of the stated conjecture; (2) Benoist-Voisin, 'On the smoothability problem with rational coefficients' (arXiv:2405.12620, accepted 20 Oct 2024, published in Rendiconti Lincei 2026), proves that an affirmative solution to a different classical problem (rational-coefficient smoothing of algebraic cycles, going back to Borel-Haefliger) would be *incompatible* with Hartshorne's conjecture being true. This is a conditional/logical link between two conjectures -- it neither proves nor disproves Hartshorne's conjecture, and settles nothing about it directly; it is evidence about a related problem's relationship to Hartshorne's conjecture, not a change to Hartshorne's conjecture itself. No AI system is mentioned in either paper's acknowledgements, methodology, or any secondary coverage found. The site 'ProofAtlas' (proofatlas.ai) styles itself as an 'AI-first mathematical research' platform and has a page mapping routes toward the Hartshorne complete-intersection conjecture, but on inspection it contains no completed proof, no new theorem, and no AI-produced mathematical result -- only a curated 'route map' of open sub-questions and an invitation for a 'hosted agent' to work on them in the future. This is infrastructure, not a finding, and does not change the status. I searched specifically for any AI/LLM claim on this conjecture (including recent high-profile AI math results like the unit distance conjecture and Erdos problem 1196) and found no connection to Hartshorne's conjectures.
competing_reading: One could argue Watanabe's n=2c-1 classification is 'about' the conjecture in a loose sense, since it directly abuts the conjectured threshold and uses the same quadratic-variety framework; if read that way it would be `partial` progress with `resolution_direction` null (a classification, not a proof/disproof). I judge it a related/adjacent problem rather than a case because n=2c-1 is explicitly outside the conjectured range (n>=2c+1) -- proving something about varieties in that range does not remove any territory from the conjecture as stated, which only makes a claim for n>=2c+1.
what_would_settle_it: A paper that proves or disproves the conjecture for some specific n>=2c+1 range not previously known (e.g., extending the codimension-2/Fano case, or improving on Ananyan-Hochster-style large-n results), or an authoritative statement that Watanabe's or a similar boundary-case result is understood by specialists as constraining the n>=2c+1 statement itself.
